1.q: The hand of Yahweh was upon me
1.note: The word “hand” is often used to refer to someone’s power or action. A person with his hand on another person has power over that other person. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 1:3. Alternate translation: [Yahweh was controlling me]

2.note: The word “Behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

3.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

4.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh speaks to Ezekiel.

4.q: Listen to the word of Yahweh

5.note: Alternate translation: [Look] or [Listen] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you]
The noun “breath” can be stated as the verb “breathe.” Alternate translation: [I will cause you to breathe]
The Hebrew word translated as “breath” in these verses is translated as “spirit” by a few modern versions. It is also translated as “wind” in Ezekiel 37:9.

6.note: the tissue that connects muscles to bones

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

7.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh had commanded me to speak]
The word “behold” here shows that Ezekiel was surprised by what he saw.

8.note: This refers to the parts of human bodies that are like hard strings and hold the bones and muscles together. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 37:6.

8.q: But there was still no breath in them
8.note: The noun “breath” can be stated as the verb “breathing.” Alternate translation: [But they were not breathing] or [But they were not alive]

9.note: “from the four directions that the wind can blow in.” This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [from every direction]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [these people that enemies and disasters have killed]

10.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [as Yahweh had commanded me]

11.note: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03).
The word “Behold” here adds emphasis to what follows. Alternate translation: [Indeed!]

The people being destroyed and removed from their land is spoken of as if they had been cut off like a person would cut off a branch or piece of cloth. Alternate translation: [Our nation is destroyed]

12.q: I will open your graves and lift you out from them
12.note: Yahweh restoring the people and bringing them back to their land is spoken of as if he will bring them back to life again.

13.note:
# General Information:

These are Yahweh’s words to the house of Israel.

14.note: Alternate translation: [to live peacefully in your own land]

Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, Yahweh, have declared]

15.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

16.note: Here “For” means “representing.” Alternate translation: [Representing Judah] or [Belonging to Judah]
The tribe of Judah lived in the southern kingdom of Israel which was called Judah. Here the name is used to refer to the whole southern kingdom.

16.q: the people of Israel, his companions
16.note: This refers to the Israelites who lived in the southern kingdom of Judah. Alternate translation: [all the tribes of Judah] or [the tribes of Israel who are part of the kingdom of Judah]

16.q: For Joseph, the branch of Ephraim
16.note: Joseph was Ephraim’s father. The tribe of Ephraim lived in the northern kingdom of Israel. Here the names are used to represent the whole northern kingdom.

16.q: all the people of Israel, their companions
16.note: This refers to the Israelites who lived in the northern kingdom of Israel. Alternate translation: [all the tribes of Israel] or [the Israelites who were part of the kingdom of Israel]

The phrase **his companion** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text in the oldest complete manuscript. There is, however, a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended and that represents the reading of some other Hebrew manuscripts. The UST follows this reading. You may want to follow this reading in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [his companions…his companions]

17.note: Alternate translation: [so that they become one stick]
Here, the word for “one” is given a plural form, and so the ULT represents this. The sense seems to be “united” or “unified.” Alternate translation: [united]

18.q: what these things of yours mean
18.note: Alternate translation: [what your sticks mean] or [why you have these sticks]

19.note: This tells the reader to pay special attention to what follows. Alternate translation: [Look!] or [Listen!] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you!]
“the stick of Joseph.” This represents the kingdom of Israel.

19.q: that is in the hand of Ephraim
19.note: The word “hand” refers to power. Alternate translation: [that is in the power of Ephraim] or [that the tribe of Ephraim rules over]

19.q: the tribes of Israel his companions
19.note: Alternate translation: [the other tribes of Israel who are his companions] or [the other tribes of Israel who are part of that kingdom]
“the stick of Judah.” This represents the kingdom of Judah.

20.note: Here the people are represented by their “eyes” to emphasize what they see. Alternate translation: [while they watched you]

21.note: Alternate translation: [Look!] or [Listen!] or [Pay attention to what I am about to tell you!]

23.q: they will be my people and I will be their God
23.note: See how you translated this in Ezekiel 11:20.

24.note: Yahweh said “David” to refer to a descendant of David. See how you translated “my servant David” in Ezekiel 34:23. Alternate translation: [A descendant of my servant David]
This speaks of a king ruling a people as if he were a shepherd leading sheep. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 34:23.
Alternate translation: [over the people of Israel]

24.q: will walk according to my decrees
24.note: This speaks of acting or behaving in a certain way as if it were a person walking. Alternate translation: [will live as I have commanded]

26.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh is speaking about the people of Israel.
Alternate translation: [I will set up] or [I will create]
“a covenant that brings peace.” See how you translated this in Ezekiel 34:25.
It was implied that Yahweh would establish them in the land of Israel. Alternate translation: [I will set them in the land of Israel] or [I will cause them to live securely in the land of Israel]
Alternate translation: [cause their people to increase in number]
Alternate translation: [my holy sanctuary] or [my holy temple]

27.note: Alternate translation: [The place where I live]

27.q: I will be their God, and they will be my people
27.note: See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 11:20.
